title: Fake Minecraft Server configuration
description: The configuration file of Fake Minecraft Server (see docs/configuration.md).

listen.description: The addresses to listen on, each one alone or with its options.

timeout.description: The maximum lifetime of a connection.

handshake_timeout.description: The time that a client has to send its handshake, and the request that follows it, after it connects (at most connections.timeout).

max.description: The maximum number of concurrent connections (0: unlimited).

max_per_ip.description: The maximum number of concurrent connections per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 (0: unlimited).

rate_limit_per_ip.description: The maximum number of new connections per second per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64, in bursts of up to twice as many (0: unlimited).

format.description: text, for people, or json, one object per line, for log collectors.

rate_limit.description: The maximum number of lines logged per second about connections (0: unlimited).

no_software_signature.description: Whether to leave out "fakeMinecraftServer":true, which statuses end with so that tools can tell this server from real ones.

upstreams.description: The real servers polled for their status, by ID.

servers.description: The servers that clients see, by ID; the default server answers the clients that no rule matches.

rules.description: Which server each client sees: the first rule that matches answers.

script.description: Functions and constants written in Starlark, for conditions and hooks.

script_file.description: The path of a file that holds the script instead, relative to the configuration file.

duration.description: A number and a unit among ms, s, m and h, such as 500ms, 3s or 1m30s.

text.description: Text with formatting codes, such as "§cRed", or a text component.

proxy_protocol.description: Whether connections start with a PROXY protocol header.

trusted_proxies.description: For TCP listeners with proxy_protocol: the addresses or CIDR prefixes allowed to send a header.

listenAddress.description: host:port (an empty host listens on every interface), or unix:path for a Unix socket.

upstream.description: The ID of the upstream whose status is shown in place of status while it answers, or "" for none (by default, the upstream with the ID of the server).

client_protocol.description: When to report the protocol version of each client in place of the one of the status.

kick.description: The message sent to players who try to join.

ping_script.description: A Starlark expression that can answer status requests in place of the status.

join_script.description: A Starlark expression that can answer players in place of the kick message.

status.description: The status shown in the server list, with the fields of the status JSON of Minecraft servers; other fields, such as the ones of mods, are sent as is.

description.description: The message of the day, on up to two lines.

favicon.description: The icon: the path of a 64×64 PNG file, or a data URI of one.

name.description: The version name, which clients show in red, in place of the player counts, when they see the server as incompatible.

sample.description: The lines shown when hovering over the player counts.

enforcesSecureChat.description: Whether the server requires signed chat messages (1.19.1+).

previewsChat.description: Whether the server previews chat messages as players type them (1.19 to 1.19.2).

address.description: host or host:port of the server, IPv6 addresses in brackets; without a port, its SRV record is followed.

host.description: The host name sent in the handshake, for proxies that route by host name (by default, the host of address).

port.description: The port sent in the handshake (by default, the port of address, or 25565).

protocol.description: The protocol version sent in the handshake; -1 asks the server for its own.

retry_interval.description: The time between two polls after a failed one (by default, 10s, or interval if shorter).

timeout.description: The maximum duration of a poll (by default, 5s, or interval if shorter).

max_age.description: How long the last status stays in use while polls fail, at least interval + timeout (by default, 3 times interval, or interval + timeout if longer).

server.description: The ID of the server that clients see.

host.description: The hosts that clients connected to, one of which must match.

name.description: The name of the rule in logs: lowercase letters, digits and underscores, not only digits, nor default.
